answer_verbatim:

Based on the results you provided, **BBS Insurance** and **HUB International Kansas City** look like the strongest broker-style options, while **Blue KC** is primarily an insurer, not a broker.[9][4][1]

| Option | Why it may fit a self-employed buyer | Notes |
|---|---|---|

| **HUB International** | Large healthcare insurance broker office in Kansas City, which can be useful if you want broader carrier access and business-oriented support.[4] | Better if you want a larger firm with more resources. |
| **HealthMarkets / licensed agent** | Connects you with a local licensed health insurance agent in Kansas City.[10] | Useful if you want help comparing marketplace options. |
| **Blue KC** | Local health insurer with Kansas City presence.[1] | Not a broker; best if you already know you want Blue KC coverage. |

If your main goal is **finding coverage as a self-employed person**, I would start with **BBS Insurance** or **HUB International** because they are broker-type providers and can help compare plans rather than selling only one insurer’s products.[9][4]

A few quick buying criteria matter more than the brand name:
- **ACA marketplace expertise**, especially if you may qualify for premium tax credits.
- **Access to multiple carriers**, so you can compare premium, deductible, and provider networks.
- **Help with self-employed income scenarios**, since income affects subsidy eligibility.
- **Local service**, if you want ongoing help with billing, claims, or plan changes.
